identity.title: Position: Irresponsible AI: big tech’s influence on AI research and associated impacts

problem.claim: The paper examines how big tech’s influence and involvement in AI research contribute to irresponsible AI development and related societal and environmental impacts.

contributions.claim: Develops an argument linking big tech’s influence to irresponsible AI through scaling incentives, general-purpose systems, and related economic forces.
Reviews current environmental and societal harms of AI and traces their connections to big tech’s influence.
Proposes researcher-oriented strategies grounded in implicated actors’ responsibility and collective action.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report examining big tech’s disproportionate influence in AI research and arguing that its scaling and general-purpose-system drive conflicts with responsible, ethical, and sustainable AI development.
The authors report reviewing environmental and societal negative impacts and tracing their connections to big tech’s influence.

narrative_sequence.summary: Big tech’s increasing presence has accelerated AI development, deployment, and adoption alongside growing ethical, societal, and environmental concerns.
The paper argues that big tech strongly drives irresponsible AI and organizes the argument around mechanisms of influence.
It examines disproportionate research influence, scaling and general-purpose systems, resulting harms, and underlying economic forces.
It calls on researchers to counter this influence through responsibility-based and collective-action strategies.

source_observation.claim: The abstract organizes a position around a causal pathway from institutional influence, through research and economic drivers, to societal and environmental impacts, followed by proposed collective responses.

lessons.interpretation: Making the pathway explicit can connect a normative thesis to concrete mechanisms and actions.
lessons.application: For a position paper, map the central claim as influence or incentive → mechanism → impact → actor-specific response, and assign each link to a distinct section.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unsuitable when the work does not make mechanism-level claims or when evidence cannot support directional links.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the reviewed impacts, economic forces, proposed strategies, or supporting sources and evidence.
It does not establish the strength, exclusivity, or empirical validity of the claimed links between big tech’s influence and irresponsible AI.
